Director Johnson asked Management Analyst Shigenaga if the minutes presented were verbatim and

audio recording is available online for review. Director Johnson then asked Management Analyst

2. CHAIRPERSON REPORT

Chairperson Hollingsworth reported meeting with Trustee Chien, Director Johnson, and

Management Analyst Shigenaga, on October 19 to set the agenda for today’s meeting and to talk
about budget and CIP. She commended Director Johnson for her efforts in developing the draft of
the Director’s Report and Staff Briefing in preparation for that meeting.

3. TRUSTEE REPORTS

No Trustee Reports were provided at this time.

4. CRAIN ART GALLERY REPORT

Vice Chairperson Mollno reported that Marian Fortunati’s work will be going up on November 6th
through the end of the year. She hopes that by the next Board meeting, the calendar for 2022 will
be solidified. Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if any changes have been made regarding receptions
for the artists. Vice Chairperson Mollno responded that no artist thus far has wanted to do a
reception, but she anticipates that receptions will be offered in 2022. She thinks it is in our best
interest to offer receptions because most sales are made during receptions. Not only does the artist
make the sale, but the Library also receives a portion of the profit in the form of a donation.

5. MARKETING AND PUBLICITY LIAISON REPORT

Trustee Domier reported no official meeting, but a discussion with Director Johnson. From that
conversation, he was encouraged by her deep background in marketing and publicity. He stated that
the Library has been doing a lot of terrific things, but those things have not been communicated to
the community at large.

He reported having a discussion with City Manager Marlowe during which they talked about the
City Manager’s Weekly Briefing. Historically in the Weekly Briefing, Community Services had only a
soccer icon next to its name to represent the Recreation Division, but City Manager Marlowe agreed
to add another icon to represent the Library Division. Director Johnson added that she will request
to add the Crowell Public Library logo to the Community Services header in the Weekly Briefing.

6. BUDGET AND CIP LIAISON REPORT

Trustee Chien reported a productive meeting with Director Johnson and Management Analyst
Shigenaga. She stated that she is feeling comforted by Staff’s level of enthusiasm and is encouraged
by their work thus far.

7. SAN MARINO CENTER RENOVATION UPDATE REPORT

No report was given. Vice Chairperson Mollno asked if the San Marino Center will be turned into
a Senior Center. She doesn’t believe there is a need for a Senior Center since most of the seniors
are in a club or organization. Trustee Domier responded that he has not heard the term “Senior
Center” used in any of the meetings he has attended. He stated that the San Marino Center will be
a Community Center serving all the needs of San Marino, regardless of age. Director Johnson added
that she will be working on revamping the Activities Guide. She plans on adding a few pages so the
Department can be a better storyteller on all major projects and initiatives in place. An update on
the San Marino Center would be included on one of these new pages. Trustee Domier
recommended talking to Mayor Ude or City Manager Marlowe to get that update.

Chairperson Hollingsworth brought up how the focus three years ago was on additional
programming for seniors through Recreation. She thinks that the idea some people have regarding
the San Marino Center becoming a Senior Center stems from that. Vice Chairperson Mollno
mentioned some concern she has heard that non-San Marino groups may come in to utilize the
space, but don’t necessarily align with the San Marino model. Director Johnson added that she
understands that the facility will service all ages with a balanced array of offerings. Chairperson
Hollingsworth added that as more Recreation programs occur at the San Marino Center, the local
schools may show interest in utilizing the space as well. Overall, she thinks it will be a well utilized
facility. Director Johnson mentioned that she is meeting with the School District again today. At the
last meeting with the School District, Director Johnson mentioned the conjoined use of the San
Marino Center and worries about parking did come up.

ADMINISTRATIVE BUSINESS

8. CITY MANAGER’S UPDATE ON MISSION STATEMENT

Chairperson Hollingsworth brought up how a few months ago, Mayor Ude suggested a review of
the Mission Statement. She acknowledged that rewriting or revising the document is a huge
undertaking. Last meeting, Chairperson Hollingsworth meant to ask City Manager Marlowe for an
update, but forgot, so she emailed City Manager Marlowe for an update.

City Manager Marlowe’s email talked about how there are plans to revise the internal organization
and departmental Mission Statements over the next year once key positions are filled. She thinks
the documents could be done in time for the FY 2022-23 budget. However, she does not have plans
for the Boards and Commissions as she believes the City’s Municipal Code lays out each body’s
charter. Any future steps would likely be guided by the research Mayor Ude is doing relating to the
role of the Board.

Chairperson Hollingsworth agreed with City Manager Marlowe in that the City should wait until
fully staffed to work on the project. However, she did not like when Staff updated the Mission
Statements last time in a one-day training without any input from the public. Chairperson
Hollingsworth expressed a desire to table this item and when Staff start working on the Mission
Statements, she would like the Trustees to be made aware. In addition, she would like the public
and the Trustees to be made aware of how they can be involved. Vice Chairperson Mollno wondered
why Staff created the last Mission Statement. She recalled the Board creating a 5-year plan that
included a Mission Statement that was submitted to City Council for approval. She noted that the
Trustees are here because they are capable of doing things for the City and can help take some of
the workload off of Staff. Vice Chairperson Mollno agreed to table this item. She went on to say that
if Staff is going to write the Mission Statement, she would at least like the opportunity for the Board
to submit a draft for consideration. Trustee Chien believes that Mission Statements are not defined
by Staff and that allowing the public and the Trustees to have an opinion would be a great way to
get everyone involved. Trustee Domier agreed that gathering feedback from the community sounds
like a good idea.

Chairperson Hollingsworth noted her response to City Manager Marlowe’s email. In her response,
she thanked City Manager Marlowe for her quick response and stated that she would share the

9. DIRECTOR’S REPORT AND STAFF BRIEFING

Director Johnson provided a walk through of the layout of her new report. She stated that the
report starts with administrative announcements, like personnel updates, followed by administrative
initiatives or projects. After that, the financials are presented. She is accustomed to giving budget
summary reports, which are very high level and different from what the Board has received in the
past. Then, she provided a 90-day snapshot of upcoming events that the Board can attend or get
involved in. This also includes office closures. Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if any Library Staff
are involved in the upcoming senior trips and Director Johnson responded that the trips are a
Recreation program. The next section she presented is the Staff Briefings, completed with the help
of full time Staff that run programs. She elaborated that the programs included have already
happened and Staff are providing an evaluation of the program. Chairperson Hollingsworth noted
that the Take and Make kits seem so popular and asked why so many people were on the waitlist
for the Batman kit. She offered to help provide materials or put together kits so that everyone who
signs up before the deadline can get a kit. Director Johnson continued to review the layout of her
report with the next section reviewing any projects that Public Works is assisting with. As soon as
the Public Works Manager starts, she hopes to finish up the interior painting and Story Walk. She
noted that in the coming months, more detailed information on social media growth will be provided.
Lastly, she shared that when Staff receive high praise or kudos, those will be shared with the Board.

Trustee Domier stated that he thinks the new layout of the report is terrific and recommended
incorporating the commendations into marketing materials. Director Johnson agreed that the
testimonials should be included in the website or the Activity Guide. Trustee Chien commented
that she liked the report and is interested to see how we grow followers on social media.

10. BUDGET & DONATION MONITOR DETAIL REPORTS

Management Analyst Shigenaga shared that when she started, she inherited all of the previous
Analyst’s files. She mentioned that she reviewed the July Board packet and saw that preliminary year
end financials were presented. So, she used the previous Analyst’s reports to enter in finalized year
end data. She said that there weren’t too many big changes, but one big change was in the Restricted
Donations Equipment line item, which covered the acquisition of 36 public access computers. She
reported preparing this fiscal year’s reports for Quarter 1. She did note that September’s books
have not been closed, so the data is still preliminary. She also noted an error on Finance’s end related
to DVD rental revenue (Line 6). DVD rental revenue was improperly coded in July, and fixed it in
September. Chairperson Hollingsworth asked if that had to do with the reallocation of DVD budget
to programs as a result of low demand. Acting City Librarian Plumley did not recall. Management
Analyst Shigenaga then continued to talk about the 3 donations received in Quarter 1 of FY 2021-
22 totaling $600. She noted that the two donations Chairperson Hollingsworth reported receiving
last meeting from the Library Foundation are not included. She believes they have not been
accounted for on Finance’s end, as their books are not yet closed. Acting City Librarian Plumley
clarified that the two donations received from the Library Foundation were for $1,000 and $2,725.
Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that the Financial Impact section on the Budget Monitor has not
been provided to the Board in the past. Management Analyst Shigenaga said that she believed that

Chairperson Hollingsworth then went on to point out to the Board that the Statistical Report on

the Statistical Report so that it is less of a demand on Staff. Vice Chairperson Mollno added that
some kind of a summary alerting the Board of any inconsistencies or red flags would be good.
Chairperson Hollingsworth recommended taking a meeting to review the Statistical Report to see
what information is desired by each Board member. Vice Chairperson Mollno noted that this report
is not something the Board may need each month, but instead quarterly. Trustee Chien added that
quarterly updates could work, but if something extraordinary happened, the Board would request
the updates more frequently.

OLD BUSINESS

11. CONSIDERATION OF RESUMING IN PERSON TRUSTEE MEETINGS

Director Johnson reported talking with City Manager Marlowe who shared that none of the City’s
Boards or Commissions are meeting in person right now. The green light to switch to in person
meetings will come from City Council. Director Johnson noted that in order to go to a hybrid
model, there is a huge staffing impact to be able to meet the Brown Act. Three Staff would need to
be trained to assist with audio, visual, and other technology logistics. Chairperson Hollingsworth
stated that the Board is happy to meet in person, but will wait for direction from City Council. Vice
Chairperson Mollno noted that participants hardly ever show up to these meetings, so worrying
about a hybrid meeting does not make sense for the Board. Chairperson Hollingsworth continued
that the Board would really like to meet in person and will even consider meeting in a larger room,
like the Barth Room, to allow for social distancing.

Proposed Agreement from San Marino Unified School District
Because SMUSD no longer provides their own library services to their students, they are
required to contract with another public agency as per the California Education Code. A draft

would be provided by the Library Division/CPL Staff to SMUSD students would include the
research and selection of library materials and coordinating the delivery of general school-age
library programming.

  The San Marino Public Library Foundation is excited to present the 2022 Bookmark

Barth Room A/V Project Update
The audio/visual issues in the Barth Room have been resolved. Both the overhead projector
and microphone are working, so DVDs and audio discs with sound can be played. The repairs
will allow the Barth Room to be used for meetings and programs, as well as rentals.

Main Entrance Door Counter
In October, it was brought to the attention of Staff that the door counter was not working.
After looking into the issue, it was made clear that the door counter had not been working
since mid-July. Acting City Librarian Plumley has connected the City’s IT services company with
the door counter company, so they can resolve this issue. More updates to come.

Passport Program
The Circulation Team processed 391 U.S. passport applications during the reporting period
between October 15 and November 16. Gross profits exceeded $15,151.

“Come Learn About Service Dogs!” Program
On October 17, Girl Scout Arden MacLaren presented a family program titled, “Come Learn
About Service Dogs!” as part of the requirements for Gold Award Project. Arden is raising a
puppy for Guide Dogs of America, and conducted small lesson for children about service dogs
and service dog etiquette. This program was very popular for the audience, complete with
activities and prizes to keep them engaged. 25 children and 31 adults attended this program.

“Book Character Pumpkin Decorating Contest” Program
For the first time, the Library invited participants of all ages to enter their pumpkin artwork
based on a book character for a chance to win a gift card to Vroman’s. Categories for entry
were Family, Ages 5-8, Ages 9-13, Ages 14-18, and Adult. Entries included such notable
characters/scenes as Pinkalicious, “Chicka Chicka Boom Boom,” and Ernie from “Sesame
Street.” A total of 9 entries were received, but unfortunately, one entry was disqualified for not
adhering to the rule of “No carving or holes.” Judges included City Manager Dr. Marcella
Marlowe, Community Services Director Cathi Johnson, and Librarian Christopher Taylor.
Library Staff look forward to continuing this new tradition next year.

Second Session of iPad Classes Wrap Up
Another successful session of iPad classes reached its end on November 17. 10 participants
attended a weekly class for 8 weeks to learn iPad basics. Throughout the session, participants
were allowed to check out iPads and take them home to practice what they learned each week.

Trustee Chien reported that her and Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth met with Management Analyst

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that the CIP portion of the report is redundant at this point
since there are no CIP projects this year. She then thanked Management Analyst Shigenaga for
meeting with herself and Trustee Chien last week.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted that Mayor Ude sent the Board an email regarding a change
in the financial reports that the Board receives and requested that Mayor Ude explain it in more
detail. Mayor Ude started off saying that part of the reason for the change is to try to save Staff time.
He noted that the City is really understaffed in a lot of areas. He continued to say that several Staff
provide financial oversight to the budget. Mayor Ude recommended that moving to a quarterly
review, in a summary mode, would be a healthy step. He added that the financials on the Library
side don’t change a lot; most of the changes observed are due to staffing.

Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth recalled the executive summary financial reports that Director
Johnson included last month in her report. She noted how on the Budget Monitor there are about
65-line items, but on the executive summary financial reports there are 7-line items. She did
acknowledge that the Board does not need all the detail provided in the Budget Monitor, but doesn’t
believe the executive summary quite does it. She continued that she recognizes that the Board’s
role is to advise the Council, but is worried that she won’t be able to provide the Council with good
advice just based on the executive summary reports. She stated that there needs to be something
in between the Budget Monitor and the executive summary financial reports that the Board can
receive. She went on to say that she trusts the Staff assigned to oversee the budget, but with the
high turnover in the past years, it has been tough to ensure nothing slips between the cracks. She
mentioned how she brought a donation to Management Analyst Shigenaga’s attention that doesn’t
appear on last year’s Donation Monitor. She recommended meeting to see how the Budget Monitor
can be modified and to also talk about the frequency of the report. She is also very interested in the
Donation Monitor and seeing if it is the best tool to track donations.

Mayor Ude added that when City develops the budget, there is much detail. However, when actual
financials are presented, they are in summary form and variances are presented with notes similar
to what was done in the executive summary financial reports. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted
that the executive summary reports do not include donations. Mayor Ude responded that
Management Analyst Shigenaga can create a schedule for donations. He added that the Board most
likely does not need the line item detail on a monthly basis. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth noted
that on the Budget Monitor, many expenditures are related to donations, which are also found in
the Donations Monitor. That is the information she would really like to see moving forward. She
added that about a year ago, they talked about changing the approach to donations in the budget
process. This conversation was never finished and nothing ever came of it. She asked why the City
is using the Friends’ money to pay for Other Contract Services, Materials & Supplies, etc. She added
that the Library heavily relies upon donations, which can get tough during times like when the Friends
couldn’t raise money. She recommended building the budget without any donations in it, and then
asking different groups to give donations for specific items.

Mayor Ude asked what the annual budgeted amount of donations is. Management Analyst Shigenaga
responded that in the current fiscal year, there is $21,000 budgeted in the various donation line
items. Mayor Ude noted that the Library’s entire budget is around $1,500,000. Vice Chairperson

Hollingsworth asked why the donations are used on such basic kinds of expenditures. She added
that we have a responsibility to the donors to spend the reserve funds before we go asking for more
money. She noted how she attended the Chinese Club gala the other weekend and thanked them
for their donation, but has no idea if we’ve spent the money yet. She would at least like to know a
plan to spend it, to make sure it is in the way the donor wants. She noted that if the donations were
not used from one year to the next, they were sucked up for general use. She would like unspent
donations to be set aside for the same purpose.

Mayor Ude understood the issues to be really related to the donations. He recommended that
Director Johnson and Management Analyst Shigenaga work to come up with a schedule of donations
and their related expenditures to be presented to the Board on a quarterly basis. Vice Chairperson
Hollingsworth asked Mayor Ude on his opinion of seeing a budget built not relying on donations and
he responded that he is indifferent since the amount of donations compared to the entire Library’s
budget is not a big number.

Trustee Mollno agreed with everything Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth said, but added that there
are sections of the Budget Monitor that the Board doesn’t necessarily need. She noted that she has
faith in Staff putting the Monitors together. She said that compared to the Staff monitoring the
budget, the Trustees are primary interested in the Library. She has no problem making the Budget
Monitor shorter by removing some line items, but she does take offense when saying the $21,000
in donations does not matter. Mayor Ude noted that he didn’t say it doesn’t matter. He meant to
say that in the scheme of the entire budget, $20,000 is not as big of a number. He suggested that
Board let Director Johnson and Management Analyst Shigenaga come back with a new donation
report. He noted that on the Budget Monitors, the Board should be looking at the variances to
effectively manage the financial aspect of the City. Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth responded that
she likes Mayor Ude’s idea of letting Director Johnson and Management Analyst Shigenaga prepare
a new report for further discussion in January. She added that on the Quarterly Reports, she would
like to see the difference between program and book purchases in Adult and Children’s Services.
She also requested that the other Trustees compare the Budget Monitor and the Quarterly Report
to see what else they would like to see in a new report.

Mayor Ude stated that Vice Chairperson Hollingsworth’s requests are healthy additions to the

that it just becomes noise and difficult to pay attention to what is important. He also mentioned that
when we ask for donations for something specific and it doesn’t get spent the way we said it would,
it makes us look bad as the people requesting the money. Trustee Derry agreed. Mayor Ude thinks
that the Board is making its way towards a healthy operating dashboard, by focusing on what actually
moves the needle, similar to what the Council receives on each department. Trustee Derry agrees
that the Board should focus on what moves the Library forward.

Director Johnson thanked Mayor Ude for facilitating this discussion. She appreciated the background
knowledge on the challenges around the tracking of donations and ensuring that donations are spent
for their intended use. She believes it is our obligation to report on that, but isn’t sure that the
existing reports are the best way of doing so. She mentioned that she has not been able to meet
with Finance Director, Paul Chung, to be able to better understand the restricted donations reserve
fund. This includes understanding why there is a balance and if there is a threshold that needs to be

maintained. She also mentioned the idea of a working meeting to Chairperson Domier and Vice
Chairperson Hollingsworth along with Management Analyst Shigenaga obtain the historic
perspective, talk about the clarifying questions, and improve the tools going forward.

Management Analyst Shigenaga experienced technical difficulties with Zoom and could not stop
screen sharing. In the meantime, Trustee Mollno provided some background on the restricted
donations reserve fund. She noted that for the Crain Art Gallery, the money in the reserve fund is

down the funds. She had to work with City Staff to make sure donations did not get absorbed into
